T4:gemma4_26b-a4b:B:simulate.fired: cell B of gemma4_26b-a4b, simulate: 52 unread final answers of 300 (more than 5%)
T4:gemma4_26b-a4b:B:simulate.note: Audited 2026-11-24 by reading the shape of all 52 answers (scripts in development/reference/control_prompt_fix_t4_audit/). Every one of the 52 follows the layout cell B asks for: reasoning, then one fenced json block that ends the answer. None is a final answer left in a place the readers do not look; both readers look in that block. 47 of the 52 blocks are not valid JSON as the model wrote them: the brackets do not balance (36 lack one closing brace, usually at the end of the last step; 11 have one or more closing braces too many). The other 5 are valid JSON, all in the sailing domain, and give each numeric fluent as a nested object ({"x": {"b0": 4}}) where the grader's trace form has one flat key per fluent; the frozen normaliser does not accept that form. So the count does not show a reader that skips a final answer; it shows a model that, asked for one JSON object, writes it with a syntax slip. The frozen grade and the second reading both count these answers as wrong, and the tool arm is graded by the same parser. Descriptive, audit only, not a registered reading and not to be quoted as a rate: when the bracket slips are mended at the point where the JSON parser stops, 25 of the 47 traces equal the oracle, 13 differ from it, 8 still do not parse and 1 is not a trace the grader accepts. Cell B's simulate rate for Gemma is therefore lower by up to about 8 points (25 of 300) for a syntax slip and not for the content of the trace. Released so that the readout can be written; the readout states this next to Gemma's cell B simulate figures. Whether the paper says anything about it is Omer's decision.
